title: Bind each journey spec to exactly one train or journey

facts.note: Playwright browser specs are recognised by the *.e2e.ts name.
Any test file; combined with the header-marker fact so a misnamed journey spec is still judged.

values: header comment marker: // Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:, // URN: test:journey:
facts.note: Requires a header-comment scanner (htmx_e2e_detector) that distinguishes header comments from string literals in the test body.

fires: A *.e2e.ts Playwright spec (new or already existing, header touched or not) has no // Train: or // Journey: header.
A test file not named *.e2e.ts carries a // URN: test:journey:… header comment but no binding header.
A journey spec header carries both a // Train: and a // Journey: line, or two // Train: lines.
A journey spec header has // Train: train:Orders (missing slug / not matching the planner's identity grammar).
doesNotFire: A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string literal and has no journey header marker.
Unit or acceptance tests carrying none of the journey markers.
Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated trees.

given: A journey spec: a `*.e2e.ts` Playwright file, or any test file whose header comments carry `// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…` or `// URN: test:journey:…`
when: the spec is present in the scanned tree (new or existing, whether or not its header was touched)
then: Its header block carries exactly one binding header — `// Train: train:<subject>:<slug>` or `// Journey: journey:<id>` — whose id matches the planner's identity grammar.
prefer: Add the binding to the header block, e.g. `// Train: train:orders:place-order` (or `// Journey: journey:buy`).
avoid: A journey spec with no binding header.
Two binding headers in one spec.
An id the planner would reject.
Renaming a spec away from *.e2e.ts to escape the check — header markers still bring it in scope.
unless: Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
Unit and acceptance tests carrying none of the journey markers are out of scope.
why: The binding is how a browser test is traced to the plan it exercises; a spec with no binding, two bindings, or an id the planner would reject cannot be traced.
evidence: htmx_e2e_detector reports zero findings for every journey spec: exactly one binding header, id matching the planner's identity grammar.
Reviewer can read the spec's header block and see a single `// Train: train:<subject>:<slug>` or `// Journey: journey:<id>` line.
verifier_detail: Scope (browser_spec): files matching *.e2e.ts run by Playwright, OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed spec is still judged.
A journey URN appearing only in a string (not in header comments) does not make a file a journey spec.
Count binding headers (`// Train:` and `// Journey:` lines) in the header block; exactly one is required. Zero or more than one is a finding.
Train grammar: `train:<subject>:<slug>`; Journey grammar: `journey:<id>`; both validated against the planner's identity grammar.
Exclude paths under node_modules, dist, build, _generated.
Applies to every in-scope journey spec in the scanned tree, not only newly added or edited ones.
audit: Original summary/name: A journey spec binds to exactly one train or journey.

additions.text: Renaming a spec away from *.e2e.ts to escape the check — header markers still bring it in scope.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming anti-pattern derived from the source's 'so a misnamed one is still judged'; makes the intent explicit for the coder.

additions.text: the spec is present in the scanned tree (new or existing, whether or not its header was touched)
additions.justification: The source states an invariant over all journey specs and has no explicit trigger event; the when clause restates that applicability without narrowing it.
